spots.name: Wild Horse Mountain Lookout

bio_facts.fact: Wild Horse Mountain is the smallest of the Glass House Mountains, rising 123 m, and lies east of the Bruce Highway so it gives views of the other peaks
A narrow sealed road (gated) runs to the top; a car park near the base gives a simple walk; a rotunda-style building with interpretive displays stands at the summit
Part of Beerburrum East State Forest, managed by Queensland Parks and Forests

Walk is about 1.4 km return from the car park (web search summary; the council page https://gallery.sunshinecoast.qld.gov.au/news/adventure-time-wild-horse-mountain-lookout-1-4km returned 404 to the fetcher)

cost.note: no fee found; free default for a lookout; state forest

spots.name: Auckland Point Lookout
spots.correct_wikipedia_title: none (no article; 'Auckland Point' is not a Queensland article). Official name now Auckland Hill Lookout

bio_facts.fact: Auckland Point gives an overview of Gladstone: harbour and harbour islands, heavy industry (Queensland Alumina, ports, power station), the marina, mountains and islands; a cafe sits at the top; a lit waterfall runs down the cliff face
Now called Auckland Hill Lookout, adjoining East Shores Parkland, with five modern viewing platforms and stairways from East Shores to three access points; Stage 2 opened August 2025
Run by Gladstone Ports Corporation

spots.name: Seventy Five Mile Beach
spots.correct_wikipedia_title: none as own article (K'gari article has a section; Wikipedia title 'K'gari')

bio_facts.fact: The 75 Mile Beach runs along most of K'gari's east coast (about 120 km) and is officially a main road; planes land on it and vehicles must give way to oncoming aircraft
Along it are the Champagne Pools, Indian Head, the Maheno wreck and Eli Creek outflow
A vehicle access permit must be bought before driving on K'gari

spots.name: Wolf Rock

bio_facts.fact: Wolf Rock is a set of four volcanic pinnacles about 2 km north-northeast of Double Island Point, off Cooloola; a popular scuba diving spot
The Queensland Government treats it as the state's most important habitat for the critically endangered grey nurse shark; fishing banned since 2003, diving allowed
Dive trips run from Rainbow Beach; depth 12-40 m, not suitable for introductory dives (deeper than 18 m)
bio_facts.source: https://wolfrockdive.com.au/ and WebSearch summary of dive listings

spots.name: Hill Inlet Lookout

bio_facts.fact: Short walk at Tongue Point on Whitsunday Island in Whitsunday Islands National Park, overlooking Hill Inlet and Whitehaven Beach; reached from Tongue Bay or Lookout Beach track
Whitehaven Beach is about 4.5 km of 98% silica sand; the view from the lookout across Hill Inlet is the one used in tourism brochures
A newer lookout platform opened in 2019 at the southern end of Whitehaven Beach (900 m each way)

spots.name: Airlie Beach Lagoon

bio_facts.fact: Open to everyone, 4,300 sq m holding 4.5 million litres of fresh, self-chlorinated water, on the Airlie Beach foreshore
Lifeguards patrol it; surrounded by grassy sunbathing spots, playgrounds and BBQ areas in the centre of town
Swimming is possible all year without a stinger suit (marine stingers in the sea Oct-May)

cost.note: council lagoon, no entry fee; 'open' vs 'entry' is for the writer (lifeguarded but ungated)
